Input and Interaction
Mobile users interact through touch, gestures, voice, and other input methods.
Design controls that are easy to tap and provide clear feedback.
Screen Size, Orientation, and Density
Mobile devices have different screen sizes, orientations, and pixel densities.
Use responsive layouts and scalable dimensions so content remains usable.
Lifecycle and Resource Constraints
Mobile apps get interrupted or killed by the OS, and run on devices with limited battery, memory, and bandwidth.
Design for graceful state resumption and lean resource use.
Security and Privacy Expectations
Mobile apps often access sensitive data like location, contacts, and camera. Request only what\'s needed and handle it transparently.
Ask for permissions only when the feature is used, and explain why each one is needed.
Context Awareness
Mobile apps can sense location, motion, and surroundings in ways stationary apps can\'t. This context should inform, not dictate, app behavior.
Handle missing or inaccurate sensor data gracefully instead of assuming it\'s always available.
Usage Patterns
Mobile users engage in short, frequent bursts rather than long sessions.
Design for quick task completion, minimal steps, and easy resumption after interruption.
